name: MLflow
tagline: A platform for experiment tracking, model management, evaluation, and LLM observability.
hook: Provides credential-free provider stubs for UI review and keeps single-tenant changes covered by workspace-aware tests.
summary: MLflow's CLAUDE.md combines local development commands with constraints for its tracking layer and contribution workflow. It explains provider stubs, coordinated dependency cooldown settings, test environments, and why unrelated changes should not share a squash-merged PR.

techniques.title: Make gated interfaces reviewable without credentials
techniques.body: The local server can substitute a fake provider CLI so authentication probes pass and the interface renders. The guide labels those stubs as development and CI tools, allowing review without real provider calls.
techniques.quote:
Features gated on an external provider/credentials can be rendered without real
keys, cost, or nondeterminism via credential-free stubs (see `dev/dev_stubs/`):

techniques.title: Preserve a wider tenancy contract during a narrow change
techniques.body: Tracking-store edits must retain workspace-aware validation even when motivated by single-tenant behavior. The accompanying rule requires matching workspace test variants.
techniques.quote: - When touching the SQLAlchemy tracking store, keep all workspace-aware paths and validations intact; never drop workspace plumbing even if the change focuses on single-tenant behavior

techniques.title: Synchronize a dependency policy across package managers
techniques.body: The repository applies a seven-day cooldown through Python, npm, and Yarn configuration. The guide also extends the policy to new npx invocations so one-off commands do not bypass it.
techniques.quote:
7-day cooldown on new package releases to guard against compromised or broken
versions that get pulled and yanked within a few days. Keep these in sync:

techniques.title: Connect patch scope to the merge strategy
techniques.body: The one-concern rule explains that squash merging combines unrelated work into one commit. That makes separate reverts and later reasoning harder, which supplies the practical reason to split changes.
techniques.quote:
since this repo squash-merges, they land as
one commit that can't be reverted piece by piece and is hard to reason about
later.

steal: Provide credential-free fixtures for gated UI states.
Test the broader tenancy contract when changing a shared store.
Apply dependency-age policy consistently across toolchains.
Explain how merge strategy affects patch scope and reversibility.
